title: Delhi Traders Ask Amit Shah to Bar Large Protests Until Diwali
excerpt: The Chamber of Trade and Industry says the October 16 Tiranga gathering at Connaught Place threatens 20 lakh retailers in the peak festive shopping window.
body:
• Delhi's Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Home Minister Amit Shah asking for large protests and marches in the capital to be barred until Diwali.
  • The immediate trigger is the proposed October 16 'Wave the Tricolour' / Tiranga gathering at Central Park, Connaught Place, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
  • CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal put the traders at risk at about 20 lakh retailers and past protest losses at more than Rs 2,000 crore, with Connaught Place, Janpath, Palika Bazaar, Khan Market and Lutyens' Delhi in the spillover zone.
  • For shoppers and traders: expect security restrictions and possible traffic disruption around Connaught Place on October 16 even if you are not attending any gathering.

Delhi's traders have asked the Union government to stop large protests in the capital until Diwali, warning that a march planned for October 16 at Connaught Place will land in the middle of the year's busiest shopping weeks. The Chamber of Trade and Industry wrote to Home Minister Amit Shah seeking a blanket prohibition on large sit-ins and marches until the festival, according to reports by The World Opinion and Report Wire.

Both reports name the same trigger, the same trade body and the same figures. The proposed gathering is described as the 'Wave the Tricolour' rally at Connaught Place on October 16, linked to the CJP's Tiranga March call. CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said about two million shop owners — 20 lakh retailers — are anxious about crowd movements through the central shopping districts.

Why traders say this Diwali is different

The festive calendar is compressed. Navratri, Ramlila and Diwali create a high-volume window in which many Delhi shops earn a disproportionate share of annual revenue and stock goods bought on credit months earlier. CTI argued that recent protests had already turned parts of the city into a lockdown-like environment, cutting footfall from local shoppers and from buyers travelling in from outside Delhi.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=n6fIGLod-dQ

Its loss estimate, carried in both reports, is more than Rs 2,000 crore for the trading community from recent disruptions. That is the trade body's figure, not an official assessment, and no government estimate was reported in either source. The areas CTI listed as exposed go well beyond the march route itself: Connaught Place, Janpath, Palika Bazaar, Khan Market and Lutyens' Delhi.

A wider traders' campaign is already under way

The letter to Shah is not the only appeal. A separate report by Nation Press described trader organisations appealing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Chief Justice of India and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over festive-season disruption, with bodies from Connaught Place, Sadar Bazar and Naya Bazar among those raising concerns.

That report adds an important distinction. Several trader voices there said they were not opposing the right to protest itself, but asking for demonstrations to move to designated venues such as Ramlila Maidan, away from commercial corridors. CTI's request to the Home Minister goes further, seeking a prohibition until Diwali rather than a relocation. The two asks now sit side by side: ban for the season, or move the venue and keep the protest.

Traders in that wider campaign also flagged a fiscal knock-on: lower festive sales mean lower GST collections, and unsold stock bought on bank loans leaves small firms carrying both rent and repayment costs into the winter.

What happens next

Neither report recorded a response from the Home Ministry, Delhi Police or the CJP to CTI's letter. The decision that matters for October 16 is permission: whether the Connaught Place gathering is allowed, moved, or denied, and what traffic and security arrangements follow.

For the diaspora, the story is a familiar Diwali-season collision in the capital: family shopping trips, wholesale buying for businesses back home and travel through central Delhi all run through the same few square kilometres as the protest. Anyone with business in Connaught Place on October 16 should check Delhi Police traffic advisories that morning before travelling in.
